args.summary: Decision: ROLLBACK canary 1.1. Evidence from the raw request log: (1) every one of the 10 5xx in the test belongs to version 1.1 — 5xx by version = {"1.1":10}, stable 1.0 had 0 across 7359 requests; (2) all 10 canary failures are on /checkout: 10/483 = 2.07% error rate vs 0/1455 (0.00%) on stable checkout, and 0 canary 5xx on any non-checkout path; (3) the failures are spread across all four 30s windows (1,3,3,3), so this is a sustained defect, not a startup blip; (4) latency is NOT the problem — canary p95 ~96ms vs stable ~95ms overall and equal per-path p50/p95/p99, so the regression is purely correctness on the revenue path. Judgement: a new, version-exclusive 5xx source on checkout directly costs orders, and the blast radius today is only the 25% of traffic the single canary pod serves; blocking the release is the cheaper error, so roll back and have the owner reproduce the checkout 500s before retrying. Note during analysis: pct(numbers, p) in this harness takes a fraction (0.95), not 95 — passing 95 returns the max-like value 323; the written claims use the fractional form.
